$comment: Names of the Bengali letters and signs when said on their own (bn-BD). Read by content/scripts/gen-audio.mjs (clips under the manifest key letter:<glyph>) and by the app (name under the glyph, letter playback). See docs/AUDIO.md, 'Letter names'.

strategies.a: the glyph alone (old behaviour; consonants come out as a bare sound)
strategies.b: glyph with the vowel spelled out: consonant + অ (কঅ); a vowel letter as is; a sign's own vowel (ি → ই); a mark on a carrier (texts.b)
strategies.d: the full spoken name: `say` if set, else `name`, else `traditional.bn` (উঙ, তালব্য শ, ই-কার, অনুস্বার, স্বরে অ); for a plain consonant the same as b
strategies.e: SSML <phoneme alphabet="ipa" ph="<ipa>"> around the glyph; experimental, bn-BD has no documented phone set

sources: Checked: Teachers' Portal (Bangladesh government a2i/DSHE), teachers.gov.bd/content/details/372282, a teacher's summary of the class-level Bangla grammar taught from NCTB books: kar names আ-কার ... ঔ-কার, ং ঃ ঁ as dependent letters, ঞ said close to ইয়, ৎ as a form of ত্, শ/ষ/স and ণ/ন sounding alike.

Checked: Wikipedia, 'Bengali alphabet' (letter-name tables with IPA): consonant name = consonant + inherent ɔ; স্বর অ, হ্রস্ব ই, দীর্ঘ ঈ; বর্গীয় জ, অন্তঃস্থ য, অন্তঃস্থ অ, তালব্য শ, মূর্ধন্য ষ, দন্ত্য স, মূর্ধন্য ণ, দন্ত্য ন; ঙ said uŋɔ~umɔ, ঞ (n)ĩjɔ; অনুস্বার, বিসর্গ, চন্দ্রবিন্দু, খণ্ড ত, হসন্ত.
Checked: r12a, Bengali orthography notes, r12a.github.io/scripts/beng/bn.html: হসন্ত (hɔsonto), বিসর্গ (bisɔrgô).

Not checked in this pass (reference to confirm against): Bangla Academy, বাংলা একাডেমি বাংলা উচ্চারণ অভিধান and প্রমিত বাংলা বানানের নিয়ম; NCTB আমার বাংলা বই class 1 (the letter pages); Hanne-Ruth Thompson, Bengali (Routledge, 2010/2012), ch. 1 on the script.

The course's own lexicon notes (content/lexicon/s01-s04) already give most of these names; this table agrees with them except where the brief's spelling was used (dontto for donto, borgiyo for borgio, shore for sworo).

letters.notes: The inherent vowel: open ɔ as in 'cauliflower', never the closed o of ও. Primers call it স্বরে অ ('vowel o') to tell it apart from অন্তঃস্থ অ (য়).
'Short i'; said the same as ঈ.
'Long i'; said the same as ই.
Named and said ri.
Closed o as in 'go'. Its clip is stored as letter:ও, so the word ও (and, also, s/he) keeps its own clip.

letters.name: উঙ
letters.kolkata: Also said umo (উমো); Wikipedia gives uŋɔ~umɔ without tying either to a region. Owner to confirm.
letters.notes: ঙ never starts a word, so its name is said with a vowel in front: u-ŋɔ.

letters.name: বর্গীয় জ
letters.notes: 'jo of the (চ) row', to tell it from অন্তঃস্থ য, which sounds the same.

letters.name: ইঁয়ো
letters.kolkata: A form with n, niyo (নিয়ো), is also heard; Wikipedia gives (n)ĩjɔ. Owner to confirm which side uses which.
letters.notes: Nasalised i + yo. Has no sound of its own at the start of a word; inside words it is n (পঞ্চাশ).

letters.name: মূর্ধন্য ণ
letters.notes: 'Retroflex no'; sounds the same as দন্ত্য ন today.

letters.name: দন্ত্য ন
letters.notes: 'Dental no', the everyday n.
Bangladesh: a clear f; pʰɔ is also heard.
The old অন্তঃস্থ ব has merged with it, so the long name is rarely needed now.

letters.name: অন্তঃস্থ য
letters.notes: 'Semivowel jo'; sounds the same as বর্গীয় জ.
The long name ('ব with a dot below') is used mainly when spelling a word aloud.

letters.name: তালব্য শ
letters.notes: 'Palatal sho'.

letters.name: মূর্ধন্য ষ
letters.notes: 'Retroflex sho'; sounds the same as শ.

letters.name: দন্ত্য স
letters.notes: 'Dental so'. In the name the letter is said with a clear s, even though স is usually sh in words.

letters.name: ডয়ে শূন্য ড়
letters.notes: 'ড with a dot below (শূন্য = zero)'. Often written ড-য়ে শূন্য ড়.

letters.name: অন্তঃস্থ অ
letters.kolkata: Some books call it অন্তঃস্থ য় (ontostho yo). Owner to confirm.
letters.notes: 'Semivowel o'.

letters.name: খণ্ড ত
letters.notes: 'Broken to'.

letters.name: চন্দ্রবিন্দু
letters.notes: 'Moon and dot'.

letters.name: হসন্ত
letters.notes: Kills the inherent vowel: ক্ is k with no vowel.
